lesson_title: The Black Powder That Turns Blue
hook_text: Stir this black powder into water: nothing. Stir it into acid: it vanishes and the liquid turns electric blue.
clip_script: This black powder is copper oxide. Stir it into water and nothing happens. It just sits there. Now stir it into warm dilute sulfuric acid. The black powder vanishes and the liquid turns a clear, bright blue. What happened? Metal oxides are bases, so they cancel acids. Acid plus metal oxide gives salt plus water. Here the salt is copper sulfate, and that is the blue. CuO plus H2SO4 gives CuSO4 plus H2O. No bubbles, no gas, just a disappearing powder and a colour change. Keep adding powder until some is left over, filter it off, gently evaporate some water and let it cool. Blue crystals grow, like tiny gemstones. Factories use the same reaction to dissolve rust off steel before galvanising, and farmers spray copper sulfate on vines to stop fungus.
visual_style: Macro shots of black powder swirling into a beaker that turns blue; a filter funnel dripping clear blue liquid; time-lapse of blue crystals growing in a dish.
pacing: A deliberate contrast at the start, a slow colour reveal, then a time-lapse crystal finish.
